{{Short description|American college basketball season}} {{Use American English|date=March 2026}} {{Use mdy dates|date=August 2023}} {{Infobox NCAA team season |year = 2022–23 |team = Wake Forest Demon Deacons |sport = Basketball |image = Wake Forest University Athletic logo.svg |image_size = |conference = Atlantic Coast Conference |division = |short_conf = ACC |CoachRank = |APRank = |record = 19–14 |conf_record = 10–10 |head_coach = [[Steve Forbes (basketball)|Steve Forbes]] |hc_year = 3rd |asst_coach1 = [[BJ McKie]] |asst_coach2 = [[Brooks Savage]] |asst_coach3 = Matt Woodley |stadium = [[Lawrence Joel Veterans Memorial Coliseum|LJVM Coliseum]] }} {{2022–23 ACC men's basketball standings}} The '''2022–23 Wake Forest Demon Deacons men's basketball team''' represented [[Wake Forest University]] during the [[2022–23 NCAA Division I men's basketball season]]. The Demon Deacons were led by third-year head coach [[Steve Forbes (basketball)|Steve Forbes]] and played their home games at the [[Lawrence Joel Veterans Memorial Coliseum]] in [[Winston-Salem, North Carolina]] as members of the [[Atlantic Coast Conference]]. They finished the season 19–14, 10–10 in [[2022–23 Atlantic Coast Conference men's basketball season|ACC play]] to finish in a tie for eighth place. As the ninth seed in the [[2023 ACC men's basketball tournament|ACC tournament]] they defeated [[2022–23 Syracuse Orange men's basketball team|Syracuse]] before losing to [[2022–23 Miami Hurricanes men's basketball team|Miami]] in the quarterfinals. ==Previous season== The [[2021–22 Wake Forest Demon Deacons men's basketball team|Demon Deacons]] finished [[2021–22 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2021–22 season]] 25–10, 13–7 in [[2021–22 Atlantic Coast Conference men's basketball season|ACC play]], to finish in fifth place. They lost to [[2021–22 Boston College Eagles men's basketball team|Boston College]] in the second round of the [[2022 ACC men's basketball tournament|ACC tournament]]. They received an at-large bid to the [[2022 National Invitation Tournament|National Invitation Tournament]], where they defeated [[2021–22 Towson Tigers men's basketball team|Towson]] and [[2021–22 VCU Rams men's basketball team|VCU]] in the first two rounds.
